MINUTES
  JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  NOVEMBER 8, 2017

  A joint adjourned meeting of the City Council and Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling
  Hills Estates was called to order at 6:00 p.m. at the City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers, 4045
  Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

  2.  OVERVIEW OF THE 60TH CITY CELEBRATION – CHAIR POPE

  CHAIR POPE stated that it was a pleasure to work with everyone involved; Betty’s Foundation and
  the Equestrian Group was amazing.

  3.  2017 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the City provided a brief summary of the staff report
  for this item and stated that this year the cost of the rental equipment was reduced by approximately
  $1K. Staff contacted Supervisor Hahn’s office who was able to provide free shuttle buses. There
  was a good turnout at the event. The volunteers did a good job promoting the event on site.

  A general discussion was held regarding the event, with some of the suggestions and concerns
  being as follows:
  • Tickets for all activities be consolidated to one booth.
  • Credit card reader for ticket sales.
  • Reconfigure space. Recommendations include: move food vendors closer to the stage
  area, move event closer to the picnic benches, move equestrian shows closer to the main
  event area, booths should be moved to face the stage.
  • Provide map for attendees.
  • Hiring an emcee for the entire event.
  • Sequential program for all activities.
  • Provide entertainment that is authentic to the City.
  • Concern that opening ceremony was not well attended.
  • Evaluate how to draw the equestrian community to the event.
  • Move equestrian events later in the day and provide a tighter program schedule.
  • Equestrian group concerned that Ernie Howlett Park may not be a good venue for their
  activities.
  • Equestrian group concerned with the footing in the arena.
  • Determine if the food vendor’s fee will be increased.
  • Suggested dates for 2018 Event – September 15th or September 22nd.
  • Separate food truck for VIP tent.
  • Activities for the kids, includes: face painting, three-legged races, water balloon toss, etc.,
  hay ride.
  • Promotions with flyer and free tickets was helpful.
  • Two-mailing promotions – “Save the Date” early and the Flyer with Tickets 10 days in
  advance.
  • Early bird ticket promotion.
  • More social media integration.
  • Volunteers wearing something identifiable (cowboy hats).

  There was a general consensus that the event remain at Ernie Howlett Park next year.

  4.  BETTY’S FOUNDATION EVALUATION

  Clint Woesner stated that the VIP attendees had a great time. Bands are contacting the
  foundation for next year’s event.

  In response to a question by CHAIR POPE, Mr. Woesner stated that most of the VIP’s were local
  residents. However, reaching the entire community could be improved.

  Karah Woesner stated that KCSN 88.5 FM was a sponsor and provided 20 spots to promote the
  event.

   COMMISSIONER GIGLIA stated that Daily Breeze and Peninsula News should have more
  coverage on the event.

  5.  FINANCIAL SUMMARY

  Community Services Director Clark reported that due to several cost reductions the
  negative financial balance was reduced by almost $5,000 this year.

  6.  ADJOURNMENT TO ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 14, 2017 AND
